title: SERVER-001: the HTTP WebSocket upgrade handler overflows websocket_key[256] when the Sec-WebSocket-Key header value exceeds 219 bytes
description:
indigo_libs/indigo_server_tcp.c:134 copies the attacker-controlled Sec-WebSocket-Key header into a fixed websocket_key[256] with strncpy (up to 255 bytes + NUL), then line 152 unconditionally strcat()s the 36-byte GUID '258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11'. A header value of 220+ bytes makes the concatenation write past the 256-byte stack buffer; the worker reads the header with indigo_uni_read_line into header[1024], so values up to ~1004 bytes reach this path from an unauthenticated TCP/HTTP client requesting '/'. Confirmed by an isolated ASan reproducer of the exact copy/append operations (control exit 0; 255-byte value aborts with stack-buffer-overflow, WRITE of size 37). Next action: assign a scoped repair task (bound the strncpy length so the buffer always leaves room for the 36-byte suffix plus NUL, e.g. copy at most sizeof(websocket_key)-37, or reject over-length keys) and reverify; owner decision required because the overflow is remotely reachable.

Imported from .factory/findings/archive/FND-000045.json (category: security, blocking: yes).
